kill.text: Price below $22: sell discipline - thesis of cheap AI-server earnings has failed
Any restatement, auditor change, late filing or new DOJ/SEC action
Gross margin below 10% for two quarters (Q1 FY27: 12.7%)
Operating cash flow negative for four straight quarters

sections.industry_map: Super Micro designs and assembles servers and rack-scale systems (GPU servers, liquid cooling, 'DCBBS' data-centre building blocks) for AI data centres, cloud providers and enterprises, mainly using Nvidia and AMD chips.
sections.size_growth: AI server market is growing 50%+ a year with hyperscaler capex. Super Micro's fiscal Q1 2027 sales were $19.9B (vs $5.0B a year earlier) and it guides fiscal 2027 sales of $72-82B (Super Micro 8-K, Nov 2026). Very cyclical: tied to GPU launch cycles and AI capex.
sections.structure: Commodity-like assembly with low margins; competitors Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Taiwanese ODMs (Foxconn, Quanta, Wiwynn). Nvidia controls supply allocation. Buyer power is high (few large customers).
sections.demand_supply: Demand very strong now; supply depends on Nvidia allocation. Bottlenecks: GPUs, power and liquid-cooling capacity. Call: strong through 2027, then exposed to any AI capex pause.
sections.industry_risks: (1) AI capex slowdown - medium/very high; warning: hyperscaler capex guides. (2) Margin squeeze from ODMs and Dell - high/high; warning: gross margin. (3) Export controls on China and Middle East - medium/medium. (4) Post-midterm data-centre policy - medium/medium.
sections.outlook: Near: revenue ~$20B a quarter, gross margin ~12-13%. Mid: margins depend on liquid cooling and DCBBS mix. Long: likely remains a low-margin assembler unless software/services grow.
sections.winners: Speed to market on new GPU platforms, liquid cooling, cost, Nvidia allocation, working-capital financing.
sections.business: Net income $1.59B and non-GAAP EPS $1.81 in Q1 FY27, but operating cash flow was -$434M; inventory $15.1B and receivables $9.7B rose sharply. Cash $6.9B vs bank debt and converts $8.6B. Figures were preliminary and unreviewed by the auditor at release.
sections.right_to_win: Super Micro is often first to ship new GPU platforms in volume and leads in direct liquid cooling.
sections.moat: None to narrow: engineering speed is real but replicable; the engine's 'Wide' reading is a scoring artefact from high recent ROIC. Trend: stable to weakening as Dell and ODMs scale.
sections.tam_competitors: ~10-15% of AI servers. Competitors: Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Foxconn, Quanta.
sections.management: Founder-CEO Charles Liang. Governance history is the key risk: 2018 delisting for late filings, 2020 SEC settlement on accounting, 2024 auditor (EY) resignation and short-seller allegations, later cleared by a special committee and a new auditor. Insider sales $15M recently.
sections.financials: Revenue $3.6B (FY21) to ~$22B (FY25) and far higher in FY27; gross margin fell from ~14% to ~11-13%. FCF negative in most recent years (-$7.0B in FY26 on the engine data) as working capital ballooned. Share count up ~6.8% a year. Short interest 14% of float.
sections.company_risks: (1) Earnings quality - KPI: operating cash flow vs net income. (2) Receivables/inventory build - KPI: days outstanding. (3) Governance - KPI: filings on time, auditor stability. (4) Customer concentration - KPI: top customer share.
sections.variant_view: The market prices SMCI at ~4x forward earnings because it does not trust the earnings; we agree the discount is mostly deserved - profits are not turning into cash and governance risk is real - so the low P/E is a value trap risk rather than a bargain.
sections.valuation: Our value (owner earnings $4.0/share haircut for cash conversion, 8% then 4%, 14% discount): low $25, base $45, high $65; price $28.8 is 36% below base. Required margin of safety 45% (cyclical) plus 10 points for governance/permanent-impairment risk = 55%, so entry $20. Street mean $43 (15 analysts). Ming's cost $28.30 (+1.5%). Verdict PASS: do not add; it is the most likely candidate to exit if cash flow does not turn positive.
sections.pillars: (1) Operating cash flow turns positive by Q3 FY27 - breach: negative for four straight quarters. (2) Gross margin above 11% - breach below 10%. (3) Clean, on-time filings - breach: any delay or restatement. (4) Revenue in the $72-82B guide range - breach: guide cut.
sections.catalysts_flow: Q2 FY27 results (early Feb 2027); 10-Q filing on time; Nvidia next-generation (Rubin) ramp. Sellers: governance-sensitive funds; shorts at 14% of float. Buyers: deep value and momentum traders on beats.
sections.premortem: (1) AI capex pause leaves SMCI with $15B of inventory to write down. (2) Accounting or governance issue resurfaces. (3) Dell and ODMs take share and margins fall below 10%.
